source_text: Sed enim ordo rationis et fidei auctoritas digestis uocibus et litteris domini admonet nos post haec credere etiam in spiritum sanctum, olim ecclesiae repromissum, sed statutis temporum opportunitatibus redditum. est enim per Ioelem prophetam repromissus, sed per Christum redditus. in nouissimis, inquit, diebus effundam de spiritu meo super seruos et ancillas meas. dominus autem: accipite spiritum sanctum; quorum remiseritis peccata, erunt remissa; et quorum retinueritis, erunt retenta. hunc autem spiritum sanctum dominus Christus modo paracletum appellat, modo spiritum ueritatis esse pronuntiat. qui non est in euangelio nouus, sed nec noue datus. nam hic ipse et in prophetis populum accusauit, et in apostolis aduocationem gentibus praestitit. nam illi ut accusarentur merebantur, quia contempserant legem: et qui ex gentibus credunt, ut patrocinio spiritus adiuuentur merentur, quia ad euangelicam peruenire gestiunt legem. differentia sane in illo genera officiorum, quoniam in temporibus differens ratio causarum: nec ex hoc tamen ipse diuersus, qui haec sic gerit, nec alter est, dum sic agit, sed unus atque ipse est, diuidens officia sua per tempora et rerum occasiones atque momenta. denique apostolus Paulus: habentes, inquit, eundem spiritum, sicut scriptum est: credidi, propter quod locutus sum, et nos credimus, ideo loquimur. vnus ergo et idem spiritus, qui in prophetis et apostolis; nisi quoniam ibi ad momentum, hic semper. ceterum ibi, non ut semper in illis inesset, hic, ut in illis semper maneret: et ibi mediocriter distributus, hic totus effusus; ibi parce datus, hic large commodatus; nec tamen ante resurrectionem’ domini exhibitus, sed per resurrectionem Christi contributus. rogabo enim aiebat, patrem, et alium aduocatum dabit uobis, ut uobiscum sit in aeternum, spiritum ueritatis. et: cum uenerit aduocatus ile, quem ego missurus sum uobis a patre meo, spiritum ueritatis, qui de patre meo procedit. et: si non abiero ego, aduocatus ille non ueniet ad uos: si autem ego abiero, remittam illum ad uos. et: cum uenerit spiritus ueritatis, ille uos diriget in omnem ueritatem. et quoniam dominus in caelos esset abiturus, paracletum discipulis necessario dabat, ne illos quodammodo pupillos, quod minime decebat, relinqueret, et sine aduocato et quodam tutore desereret. Hic est enim qui ipsorum animos mentesque firmauit, qui -euangelica sacramenta distinxit, qui in ipsis illuminator rerum diuinarum fuit, quo confirmati pro nomine domini nec carceres nec uincula timuerunt; quin immo ipsas saeculi potestates et tormenta calcauerunt, armati iam scilicet per ipsum atque firmati, habentes in se dona, quae hic idem spiritus ecclesiae Christi sponsae quasi quaedam ornamenta distribuit et dirigit. hic est enim qui prophetas in ecclesia constituit, magistros erudit, linguas dirigit, uirtutes et sanitates facit, opera mirabilia gerit, discretiones spirituum porrigit, gubernationes contribuit, consilia suggerit, quaeque alia sunt charismatum dona componit et digerit; et ideo ecclesiam domini undique et in omnibus perfectam et consummatam facit. Hic est qui in modum columbae, posteaquam dominus baptizatus est, super eum uenit et mansit, habitans in solo Christo plenus et totus, nec in aliqua mensura aut portione mutilatus, sed cum tota sua redundantia cumulate distributus et missus, ut ex illo delibationem quandam gratiarum ceteri consequi possint, totius sancti spiritus in Christo fonte remanente, ut ex illo donorum atque operum uenae ducerentur, spiritu sancto in Christo affluenter habitante. hoc etenim iam prophetans Esaias aiebat: et requiescit, inquit, super eum spiritus sapientiae et intellectus, spiritus consili et uirtutis, spiritus scientiae et pietatis, et implebit eum spiritus timoris dei, hoc idem atque ipsum et alio in loco ex persona ipsius domini: spiritus domini super me; propter quod unxit me, euangelizare pauperibus misit me. similiter Dauid: propterea unxit te, deus, deus tuus oleo laetitiae a consortibus tuis. de hoc apostolus Paulus: guz enim spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est eius; et: vbi spiritus domini, tht libertas. Hic est qui operatur ex aquis secundam natiuitatem, semen quoddam diuini generis, et consecrator caelestis natiuitatis, pignus promissae hereditatis, et quasi chirographum quoddam aeternae salutis; qui nos dei faciat templum, et nos eius efficiat domum. qui interpellat diuinas aures pro nobis gemitibus ineloquacibus, aduocationis implens officia, et defensionis exhibens munera, inhabitator corporibus nostris datus, et sanctitatis effector; qui id agens in nobis ad aeternitatem et ad resurrectionem immortalitatis corpora nostra producat, dum illa in se assuefacit cum caelesti uirtute misceri, et cum spiritus sancti diuina aeternitate sociari. erudiuntur enim in illo et per ipsum corpora nostra ad immortalitatem proficere, dum ad decreta ipsius discunt se moderanter temperare. hic est enim "qui contra carnem desiderat, quia caro contra ipsum repugnat. hic est qui inexplebiles cupiditates coercet, immoderatas libidines frangit, illicitos ardores exstinguit, flagrantes impetus uincit, ebrietates reicit, auaritias repellit, luxuriosas comissationes fugat, caritates nectit, affectiones constringit, sectas repellit, regulam ueritatis expedit, haereticos reuincit, improbos foras exspuit, euangelia custodit. De hoc idem apostolus: on enim spiritum mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex deo est. de hoc exsultat, et dicit: puto autem quia et ego spiritum dei habeo. de hoc dicit: et spiritus prophetarum prophetis subiectus est. de hoc refert: spiritus autem manifeste dicit, quia in nouissimis temporibus recedent quidam a fide, attendentes spiritibus seductoribus, doctrinis daemoniorum, in hypocrisi mendacia loguentium, cautertatam in hoc spiritu positus nemo umquam dicit anathema Iesum: nemo negauit Christum dei filium, aut repudiauit creatorem deum: nemo contra scripturas ulla sua uerba depromit: nemo alia et sacrilega decreta constituit: nemo diuersa iura conscribit. in hunc quisquis blasphemauerit, remissionem non habet, non tantum in isto saeculo, uerum etiam nec in futuro. hic in apostolis Christo testimonium reddit, in martyribus constantem fidem religionis ostendit, in uirginibus admirabilem continentiam signatae castitatis includit, in ceteris incorrupta et incontaminata doctrinae dominicae iura custodit, haereticos destruit, peruersos corrigit, infideles arguit, simulatores ostendit, improbos quoque corrigit, ecclesiam incorruptam et inuiolatam perpetuae uirginitatis et ueritatis sanctitate custodit.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed the order of reason and the authority of faith, with the words and letters of the Lord digested, admonish us to believe also in the Holy Spirit, once promised to the church, but given at the opportune times established. For He is promised through the prophet Joel, but given through Christ. In the last days, He says, I will pour out of my Spirit upon my servants and handmaids. But the Lord says: receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they will be forgiven; and whose you retain, they will be retained. But the Lord Christ calls this Holy Spirit now the Paraclete, now the Spirit of truth. Who is not new in the gospel, but neither given newly. For this same Spirit accused the people in the prophets, and provided advocacy to the nations in the apostles. For they deserved to be accused, because they despised the law: and those who believe from the nations deserve, that they may be helped by the patronage of the Spirit, because they strive to attain the evangelical law. There is indeed a difference in that one, in the kinds of duties, because in times the reason of causes differs: nor is He Himself diverse, who does these things, nor is He another, while doing thus, but one and the same, dividing His duties through times and occasions and moments. Finally, the apostle Paul says: having the same Spirit, as it is written: I believed, on account of which I spoke, and we believe, on account of which we speak. Therefore, one and the same Spirit, who is in the prophets and apostles; unless because there, at the moment, here always. Moreover, there, not as if He were always in them, here, that He may remain always in them: and there, distributed in moderation, here, poured out entirely; there, given sparingly, here, bestowed liberally; nor indeed was He exhibited before the resurrection of the Lord, but contributed through the resurrection of Christ. For I will ask, He was saying, the Father, and He will give you another Advocate, that He may be with you in eternity, the Spirit of truth. And: when the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from my Father. And: if I do not go away, that Advocate will not come to you: if indeed I go away, I will send Him to you. And: when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. And because the Lord was about to go away into the heavens, He was necessarily giving the Paraclete to the disciples, lest He leave them in some way as orphans, which was not fitting, and desert them without an Advocate and a certain guardian. For this is He who strengthened their souls and minds, who distinguished the evangelical sacraments, who was the illuminator of divine things in them, by whom, confirmed in the name of the Lord, they did not fear prisons nor chains; nay, they even trampled upon the powers of the world and torments, armed and strengthened already through Him, having in themselves the gifts, which this same Spirit distributed and directed to the church of Christ, the bride, as if certain ornaments. For this is He who established prophets in the church, taught masters, directed languages, made virtues and healings, worked miraculous works, extended discernments of spirits, contributed governances, suggested counsels, and composed and arranged the other gifts of charisms; and therefore makes the church of the Lord perfect and consummated everywhere and in all things. This is He who, in the form of a dove, came upon Him and remained, after the Lord was baptized, dwelling in Christ alone, full and entire, nor mutilated in any measure or portion, but distributed and sent with all His redundancy, that the others may receive a certain libation of graces from Him, the fountain of the whole Holy Spirit remaining in Christ, that from Him the veins of gifts and works may be drawn, the Holy Spirit dwelling abundantly in Christ. For already prophesying, Isaiah was saying: and the Spirit of wisdom and intelligence rests upon Him, the Spirit of counsel and virtue, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, and He will fill Him with the Spirit of the fear of God, this same and identical Spirit, and in another place, in the person of the Lord Himself: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me; on account of which He anointed me, He sent me to evangelize the poor. Similarly, David: therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy, beyond your companions. About this, the apostle Paul says: for whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ, this one is not His; and: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. This is He who works a second birth from water, a certain seed of divine generation, and the consecrator of heavenly birth, a pledge of the promised inheritance, and as if a certain chirograph of eternal salvation; who makes us the temple of God, and makes us His house. Who intercedes for us with divine ears, with inarticulate groans, filling the duties of advocacy, and exhibiting the gifts of defense, given to inhabit our bodies, and the effecter of sanctity; who, doing this in us, produces our bodies to eternity and to the resurrection of immortality, while He accustoms them to be mixed with heavenly virtue, and to be associated with the divine eternity of the Holy Spirit. For our bodies are instructed in Him and through Him to proceed to immortality, while they learn to temper themselves moderately according to His decrees. This is He who desires against the flesh, because the flesh resists Him. This is He who restrains insatiable desires, breaks immoderate lusts, extinguishes illicit ardors, conquers flaming impulses, rejects drunkenness, repels avarice, flees luxurious revelries, binds charities, constrains affections, repels sects, expedites the rule of truth, conquers heretics, spits out the wicked, guards the gospels. About this same Spirit, the apostle says: for we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God. About this, he exults and says: but I think that I also have the Spirit of God. About this, he says: and the Spirit of prophets is subject to prophets. About this, he reports: but the Spirit explicitly says, that in the last times some will depart from the faith, giving attention to seducing spirits, to the doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy, caution has been placed in this Spirit, so that no one ever says anathema to Jesus: no one denied Christ, the Son of God, or repudiated the Creator God: no one brings forth words against the Scriptures: no one constitutes other and sacrilegious decrees: no one writes diverse laws. Whoever blasphemes against this Spirit will not have remission, not only in this age, but also not in the future. This Spirit renders testimony to Christ in the apostles, shows constant faith of religion in the martyrs, includes admirable continence of sealed chastity in virgins, guards the incorrupt and uncontaminated rights of the Lord's doctrine in others, destroys heretics, corrects the perverse, accuses the faithless, shows hypocrites, corrects the wicked, guards the church incorrupt and inviolate, in the sanctity of perpetual virginity and truth.
pass_b_english: The order of reason and the authority of faith, once we have taken in the Lord's own words and letters, urge us to believe also in the Holy Spirit. He was promised to the church long ago, but given at the times God appointed. He is promised through the prophet Joel, but given through Christ. "In the last days," God says, "I will pour out my Spirit on my servants and handmaids" (Joel 2:28-29). And the Lord himself said, "Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you retain them, they are retained" (John 20:22-23). The Lord Christ calls this same Spirit now the Paraclete, now the Spirit of truth. He is not new in the gospel, nor was he given anew. For this very Spirit accused the people through the prophets, and through the apostles he gave advocacy to the nations. The people deserved accusation because they had despised the law; the Gentiles who believe deserve the Spirit's patronage because they strive to attain the law of the gospel. There is a real difference in the kinds of duties he performs, because the reason for his action changes with the times. Yet he himself is not different, nor does he become another; he remains one and the same, dividing his offices across times, occasions, and moments. As the apostle Paul says, "Having the same Spirit... as it is written: 'I believed, therefore I spoke,' we also believe, therefore we also speak" (2 Cor 4:13). So it is one and the same Spirit who is in the prophets and the apostles — only there he was present for a moment, here he abides always. There he was not given to stay in them permanently; here he is given to remain in them always. There he was distributed in measure; here he is poured out fully. There he was given sparingly; here he is bestowed lavishly. He was not bestowed before the Lord's resurrection, but was given through Christ's resurrection. For Jesus said, "I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate to be with you forever, the Spirit of truth" (John 14:16-17). And: "When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father" (John 15:26). And: "If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you" (John 16:7). And: "When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth" (John 16:13). Because the Lord was about to ascend to heaven, he necessarily gave the Paraclete to the disciples, so he would not leave them like orphans — which would be unfitting — abandoning them without an Advocate and guardian. This is the One who strengthened their souls and minds, who distinguished the gospel sacraments, who was the illuminator of divine things in them. Confirmed by him in the Lord's name, they feared neither prisons nor chains; indeed they trampled the powers of the world and its torments, armed and strengthened through him, bearing the gifts which this same Spirit distributes and directs to Christ's church, the bride, as her ornaments. He is the One who establishes prophets in the church, teaches teachers, directs tongues, produces virtues and healings, works miracles, extends discernment of spirits, supplies governance, suggests counsels, and composes and arranges all the other charismatic gifts — thus making the Lord's church perfect and complete in every way and everywhere.

This is the One who, in the form of a dove, came upon Jesus and remained after his baptism, dwelling in Christ alone, full and entire, not mutilated in any measure or portion, but distributed and sent with all his abundance. He did this so that others might receive a share of grace from him, while the fountain of the whole Holy Spirit remains in Christ, so that from him the veins of gifts and works may flow, the Holy Spirit dwelling abundantly in Christ. For Isaiah already prophesied this: "The Spirit of wisdom and understanding shall rest on him, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, and he will fill him with the Spirit of the fear of God" (Isa 11:2-3). This same identical Spirit speaks in another place in the person of the Lord himself: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor" (Luke 4:18). Similarly David: "Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy beyond your companions" (Ps 45:7). About this the apostle Paul says: "Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him" (Rom 8:9); and: "Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom" (2 Cor 3:17). This is the One who works a second birth from water, a seed of divine generation, and the consecrator of heavenly birth, a pledge of the promised inheritance, and as it were a deed of eternal salvation. He makes us God's temple and his house. He intercedes for us before God with inarticulate groans, fulfilling the office of advocacy and exhibiting the gifts of defense. He is given to inhabit our bodies and to effect our sanctification. Doing this in us, he brings our bodies to eternity and to the resurrection of immortality, accustoming them to be mixed with heavenly virtue and associated with the divine eternity of the Holy Spirit. For our bodies are instructed in him and through him to advance toward immortality, as they learn to govern themselves moderately according to his decrees. This is the One who opposes the flesh, because the flesh resists him. He restrains insatiable desires, breaks immoderate lusts, extinguishes illicit passions, conquers flaming impulses, rejects drunkenness, repels avarice, drives out luxurious revelries, binds charities, constrains affections, repels sects, establishes the rule of truth, conquers heretics, casts out the wicked, guards the gospels. About this same Spirit the apostle says: "We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God" (1 Cor 2:12). He exults: "I think that I also have the Spirit of God" (1 Cor 7:40). He says: "The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets" (1 Cor 14:32). He reports: "The Spirit explicitly says that in later times some will depart from the faith, paying attention to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through the hypocrisy of liars" (1 Tim 4:1-2). Caution is placed in this Spirit so that no one ever says 'Anathema' to Jesus: no one denies Christ the Son of God, or repudiates the Creator God; no one speaks words against the Scriptures; no one establishes other sacrilegious decrees; no one writes divergent laws. Whoever blasphemes against this Spirit has no forgiveness, not only in this age but also in the age to come. This Spirit bears witness to Christ in the apostles, shows the constant faith of religion in the martyrs, seals admirable continence of chastity in virgins, guards the incorrupt and uncontaminated rights of the Lord's doctrine in all others, destroys heretics, corrects the perverse, accuses the faithless, exposes hypocrites, corrects the wicked, and guards the church incorrupt and inviolate in the holiness of perpetual virginity and truth.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological distinctions of Novatian regarding the Holy Spirit's presence in the prophets versus the church. All scripture citations in Pass B match the Latin text and the required identification rule. For example, 'in nouissimis diebus' is correctly identified as Joel 2:28-29, and 'spiritus sapientiae et intellectus' as Isaiah 11:2-3. The translation of 'chirographum' as 'deed' and 'libationem' as 'share' (though 'libation' is more literal, 'share' is a valid semantic rendering in context) preserves the sense. The distinction between 'ibi' (there) and 'hic' (here) is maintained throughout.
source: 'in nouissimis diebus effundam de spiritu meo super seruos et ancillas meas.', english: 'In the last days, He says, I will pour out of my Spirit upon my servants and handmaids.'
